newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port '96 container traffic up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port '96 container traffic up sharply.

text.p: The Colombo port, south Asia's trans-shipment hub, handled a record 1,356,302 containers in 1996, up 29 percent from the year before, Sri Lanka's Ports and Shipping Ministry said on Thursday.
Transhipment traffic, which accounts for 70 percent of the port's throughput, rose by a hefty 39.6 percent, a ministry statement said.
"The port of Colombo has clearly captured an additional share from the regional transhipment market," it said.
Total cargo volume handled by Colombo rose 20 percent to 20.9 million tonnes in 1996, from 17.4 million tonnes in 1995, it said.
Container traffic rose because of the entry of new consortium and shipping lines in 1996, the statement said.
The Sri Lanka Ports Authority, which runs Colombo port, expects to reach a target of 1,550,000 containers this year, it said.
